# Adjudication Task — Chapter 453

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃453화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“야! 이 개애새끼들아아!”
  6|
  7|순간 차가운 바람이 불었던 것 같다. 아니면 내 고함이 그렇게 느껴질 만큼 우렁찼거나.
  8|
  9|아마 후자일 가능성이 크겠지.
 10|
 11|솨아아아아.
 12|
 13|은자를 줍기 위해 버둥거리던 수십 명의 사람이 움직임을 멈추고, 소란스러운 대로변에 침묵이 내려앉는다.
 14|
 15|그리고 다음 순간, 내 입술 사이로 흘러나온 한마디가 짧은 정적을 깨트렸다.
 16|
 17|“셋 센다.”
 18|
 19|“……?”
 20|
 21|“집합.”
 22|
 23|“……!”
 24|
 25|서당 개 삼 년이면 풍월을 읊고, 맞으면서 지내면 사서삼경도 외운다.
 26|
 27|그것이 지난 일 년 동안 내 폭력과 욕설에 길든 서당 개, 아니 혁무진이 누구보다 빠르게 움직일 수 있는 이유였다.
 28|
 29|“집하아압!”
 30|
 31|비명 같은 복명복창과 함께 달려온 혁무진의 신형이 내 앞에서 딱 멈췄다.
 32|
 33|이어 한 박자 늦게 사태를 파악하고 경신법을 발휘한 궁기방이 혁무진과 거의 동시에 도착했고, 청풍은…….
 34|
 35|“전병! 전병 빨리 주세요! 은인 화났어요!”
 36|
 37|시벌 놈이. 그 와중에 전병 챙기는 것 봐라.
 38|
 39|나는 군것질거리를 포장한 뒤 빛살처럼 달려오는 청풍을 향해 부드럽게 말했다.
 40|
 41|“천천히 와. 나 화 안 났으니까.”
 42|
 43|“와아! 정말요?”
 44|
 45|“응. 화난 게 아니라 존나 빡친 거야.”
 46|
 47|“앗, 아앗…….”
 48|
 49|나는 안절부절못하는 청풍과 슬그머니 시선을 회피하는 두 녀석을 바라보며 생각했다.
 50|
 51|‘도대체 이 자식들은 언제쯤 사람이 될까.’
 52|
 53|젖 먹던 힘까지 끌어 올려서 제갈세가로 달려가진 못할망정, 은자 몇 개 줍겠답시고 무공까지 쓰는 꼬락서니 봐라.
 54|
 55|심지어 궁기방 저놈은 은근슬쩍 다른 사람 손에 있던 은자까지 뺏었다. 이 정도면 거지가 아니라 도적놈이다.
 56|
 57|‘인생, 씨바…….’
 58|
 59|최근 사원 복지를 위해 애썼건만, 결국 이렇게 되는구나.
 60|
 61|맑은 하늘을 우러러본 나는 손바닥에 침을 뱉었다.
 62|
 63|“혁무진. 이마 대.”
 64|
 65|“예?”
 66|
 67|고개를 번쩍 든 혁무진이 황당한 표정으로 되물었다.
 68|
 69|“저만요?”
 70|
 71|“응. 우선 너만.”
 72|
 73|“궁 소협은요?”
 74|
 75|“쟨 뼛속까지 거지잖아. 솔직히 거지가 은자 줍는다는데 뭐라 하기도 그래.”
 76|
 77|“정확하고도 현명한 판단이로군.”
 78|
 79|눈치를 보고 있던 궁기방이 엄숙한 목소리로 끼어들자 혁무진이 고리눈을 떴다.
 80|
 81|“아니, 그렇긴 뭐가 그럽니까. 내가 거지라고 하면 맨날 화내면서.”
 82|
 83|“내가? 무슨 말도 안 되는 소릴. 나는 머리부터 발끝까지 거지다. 태어날 때부터 거지였고 죽을 때까지 거지로 살 거야.”
 84|
 85|“……거지 같네, 진짜.”
 86|
 87|“칭찬 고맙군.”
 88|
 89|“궁기방 거지새끼.”
 90|
 91|“허어, 이리도 감미로울 수가.”
 92|
 93|궁기방을 죽일 듯이 노려보던 혁무진이 재차 입을 열었다.
 94|
 95|“그럼 청 소협은요?”
 96|
 97|“청풍은 청풍이잖아.”
 98|
 99|화산파고 자시고, 청풍은 원래 저런 놈이다.
100|
101|모든 것이 함축된 한마디에 혁무진이 중얼거렸다.
102|
103|“어이가 없는데 납득이 되네…….”
104|
105|“보는 눈 많다. 빨리 끝내자.”
106|
107|“몇 대요?”
108|
109|“말해 봐. 네가 몇 대를 맞으면 반성할 수 있을지.”
110|
111|“그럼 한 대?”
112|
113|“세 대.”
114|
115|“빌어먹을, 알겠습니다.”
116|
117|“욕했으니까 다섯 대.”
118|
119|“……그냥 열 대 때리십쇼. 맞고 뒈지게.”
120|
121|“무인다운 결연한 태도에 가산점 부여한다. 그러니까 한 대. 몇 대?”
122|
123|“한 대!”
124|
125|힘차게 복명복창 한 혁무진이 이마를 내민 바로 그 순간이었다.
126|
127|“거기, 멈추도록.”
128|
129|“……?”
130|
131|나는 손바닥을 내리며 돌아섰다.
132|
133|쥐죽은 듯이 조용한 대로변의 한복판. 사인교에 올라탄 열 명의 남녀가 불쾌와 흥미로움이 뒤섞인 시선으로 이쪽을 바라보고 있었다.
134|
135|그리고 자신들의 막대한 부를 과시하듯, 하나같이 호화로운 차림새를 한 그들 중에서도 유난히 눈에 띄는 한 청년이 있었다.
136|
137|조금 전 내가 들었던 목소리의 주인이다.
138|
139|“멈췄다. 왜?”
140|
141|내 물음에 청년이 눈을 동그랗게 떴다. 자신이 들은 말을 믿을 수 없는지, 한동안 눈을 깜빡이던 그가 이내 피식 웃었다.
142|
143|“본 공자가 누구인지 모르는 모양이군.”
144|
145|“내가 그것까지 알아야 하나?”
146|
147|“이런 오만방자한 놈을 보았나!”
148|
149|청년이 한 말이 아니다. 나는 사인교를 박차고 솟구치는 신형을 바라보았다.
150|
151|‘이건 또 뭐야.’
152|
153|쉬쉭, 차창!
154|
155|공중에서 세 차례나 제비를 돌며 착지한 뱁새눈의 사내가 타오르는 눈빛으로 검을 뽑았다.
156|
157|그 화려한 동작에 지켜보던 사람들 사이에서 탄성이 터져 나온다.
158|
159|“보아하니 떠돌이 무림인 같은데, 백주대낮에 소란을 일으키는 것으로도 모자라 감히 존귀하신 분께 망발을 내뱉…….”
160|
161|“보석 많이 박았네. 그거 시선 교란용이냐?”
162|
163|나는 검을 장식한 보석을 응시했다. 종류도 다양한 수십여 개의 보석들이 햇빛을 받아 빛을 뿜어내는 중이었다.
164|
165|“뭐?”
166|
167|“눈부시니까 집어넣으라고.”
168|
169|따앙-!
170|
171|뱁새눈의 사내가 눈을 부릅떴다.
172|
173|내가 쏘아 보낸 탄지(彈指)의 힘을 이기지 못하고 손아귀를 빠져나간 검이 허공을 날아 지면 깊숙이 꽂혔다.
174|
175|“썅노무 새끼가 어디서 함부로 검을 들이대. 그것도 이런 백주 대낮에.”
176|
177|‘어쭈, 지랄한다.’
178|
179|일류 언저리쯤 되려나?
180|
181|나름대로 실력을 갈고닦은 것 같긴 한데, 극한의 겉멋충이 따로 없다.
182|
183|“이, 이놈이……!”
184|
185|“그리고 시끄럽게 군 건 너희지, 난 조용하게 만든 거고. 피차 일 복잡하게 만들지 말고 가라. 응?”
186|
187|진심이었다.
188|
189|지금까지 날파리 한두 마리 꼬여 본 줄 아나. 내 집도 아니고 지나가는 길이라면 굳이 달려드는 모기에 에프킬라까지 뿌릴 이유가 없다.
190|
191|손으로 휘휘 젓고 가던 길이나 마저 가는 게 낫지.
192|
193|하지만 아무리 진심을 전하려고 해도, 꼭 한 번에 알아듣지 못하는 놈들이 있기 마련이다.
194|
195|차차차창!
196|
197|수십 개의 검신이 사방에서 빛났다. 청색 비단 무복을 걸친 청협방의 무인들이 우리를 겹겹이 에워싸자, 당황했던 뱁새눈의 얼굴 위로 득의양양한 기색이 떠올랐다.
198|
199|“제법 알려진 낭인 놈 같은데, 지금이라도 무릎을 꿇고 용서를 빌어라. 혹시 아느냐, 공자께서 너그러이 자비를 베푸실지.”
200|
201|나는 뱁새눈의 어깨너머를 힐끗 바라보았다. 우두머리 격으로 보이는 청년을 필두로, 다른 남녀들이 반짝이는 시선으로 이곳을 바라보고 있었다.
202|
203|저건 아무리 봐도 동물원 원숭이를 구경하는 관람객의 모습이다.
204|
205|“글쎄, 저쪽은 딱히 그럴 생각이 없어 보이는데?”
206|
207|“뭐?”
208|
209|“물론 나도 그럴 생각은 없고. 그리고 지금까지 경험해 본 바로는 이게 가장 특효약이더라고. 안 그러냐?”
210|
211|슬쩍 주먹을 들어 올리자 내 눈치만 살피고 있던 버뮤다 삼각지대가 격하게 호응했다.
212|
213|“그렇지. 복날 개처럼 맞아야 정신을 차리지.”
214|
215|“그 특효약 제일 처음으로 먹은 게 저였습니다. 바로 완치됐죠.”
216|
217|“은인, 저 그럼 잠깐 만두 사러 다녀와도 돼요?
218|
219|“아니. 그냥 있어. 어차피 금방 끝날 테니까.”
220|
221|저벅.
222|
223|“자, 잠깐!”
224|
225|한 걸음을 내딛자 뱁새눈의 눈동자에 다급함이 서렸다.
226|
227|삼류 건달패라면 상대의 수준을 모르니 오기로라도 달려들겠지만, 저 녀석은 일정 수준의 무공을 익힌 무인이다.
228|
229|그렇기에 꽃병풍 역할을 하는 청협방 무인들도, 자신도 내 상대가 되지 못할 거라는 사실을 깨달은 것이 분명했다.
230|
231|“우, 우린 청협방(靑俠房)이다!”
232|
233|“어. 그래서?”
234|
235|“아, 아니 청협방의 위명을 듣지 못했단 말이냐!”
236|
237|“응. 내가 요새 귀가 잘 안 들려서.”
238|
239|저벅.
240|
241|“멈춰! 멈추라니까!”
242|
243|“크흠.”
244|
245|이렇게 되자 다급해진 것은 뱁새눈뿐만이 아니었다.
246|
247|혀를 차며 상황을 지켜보던 제갈세가의 가솔이 헛기침과 함께 입을 열었다.
248|
249|“제가 사정을 설명할 테니, 그만하시는 것이 좋을 듯 합…….”
250|
251|뻑! 털썩!
252|
253|“예? 혹시 방금 뭐라고 하셨어요?”
254|
255|“…….”
256|
257|주먹을 쥐고 우뚝 서 있는 나와, 코뼈가 주저앉은 채 혼절한 뱁새눈을 번갈아 바라보던 제갈세가의 가솔이 떨떠름하게 중얼거렸다.
258|
259|“멈추시는 게 좋을 것 같다고…….”
260|
261|“예?”
262|
263|“아무래도 이것저것 문제의 여지가…….”
264|
265|“예?”
266|
267|“괜한 충돌은 삼가시는 편이…….”
268|
269|“뭐요?”
270|
271|“……아닙니다.”
272|
273|“아, 예.”
274|
275|피 묻은 주먹을 바짓단에 문질러 닦은 나는 주위를 돌아보았다.
276|
277|궁기방은 저놈 저렇게 될 줄 알았다며 중얼거리고 있었고, 덕분에 목숨을 연장한 혁무진의 표정은 밝았다.
278|
279|그리고 청풍은…….
280|
281|“마! 어디 가!”
282|
283|“헉, 은인!”
284|
285|아니, 저 새끼 설마 지금 만두 사러 가는 거……?
286|
287|기척도 내지 않고 슬금슬금 멀어지고 있는 청풍의 뒷모습을 보니 저게 정말 사람인지 의문이 들 정도다.
288|
289|‘저 자식은 반드시 잡는다.’
290|
291|결연한 의지와 함께 걸음을 떼자, 주위를 둘러싸고 있던 꽃병풍 무인들이 헛숨을 삼키며 길을 비켰다.
292|
293|하지만 이 자리에 있는 청협방의 무인은 비단 그들뿐만이 아니었다.
294|
295|“으하하! 재미있군, 재미있어. 너희도 그리 생각하지 않느냐?”
296|
297|웃음을 터트린 청년의 물음에, 사인교(四人轎)를 짊어지고 있던 네 사람의 거한이 한 목소리로 대답했다.
298|
299|“예, 주군.”
300|
301|“이런 웃음을 준 귀인을 이리 보낼 수는 없지. 본 공자는 괜찮으니, 어서 가서 모셔오거라.”
302|
303|“충(忠)!”
304|
305|공력이 충만한 외침. 동시에 사인교를 내려놓은 거한들이 바람과도 같은 속도로 나를 향해 쇄도했다.
306|
307|일개 가마꾼에서 뛰어난 절정 고수로 변모한 그들이 사방(四方)을 점하며 달려들었다.
308|
309|후우우우웅!
310|
311|강맹한 기운이 실린 각각의 일권(一拳)이 정교하게 맞물리며 휘둘려진 그 순간.
312|
313|퍼버버벅!
314|
315|정확히 네 번의 타격음과 함께, 네 개의 몸뚱어리가 달려든 속도 그대로 엎어졌다.
316|
317|그리고 다시는 일어나지 못했다.
318|
319|“뭐여, 시부럴.”
320|
321|“……!”
322|
323|“……!”
324|
325|“……!”
326|
327|완전한 정적이 찾아온 대로변.
328|
329|의식을 잃은 거한들을 툭툭 걷어찬 내가 청년을 향해 어깨를 으쓱해 보였다. 한껏 올라갔던 그의 입꼬리는 어느새 파르르 떨리고 있었다.
330|

[P29]

[P45]

Whoosh, clang!

Clang!

Step.

[P118]

[P119]
“Yeah. So?”

[P120]
“H-have you never heard of Qingxia Hall’s reputation?”

[P121]
“Nope. My hearing hasn’t been too good lately.”

[P122]
Step.

“Stop! I said stop!”

[P124]
“Ahem.”

Whack! Thud!

[P130]
“……”

He muttered awkwardly,

[P133]

[P134]
“Pardon?”

[P135]
“There may be various complications…”

[P136]
“Pardon?”

[P137]
“It would be wise to avoid any unnecessary conflict…”

[P138]
“What was that?”

[P139]
“……Never mind.”

[P140]
“Ah. All right.”

[P142]

[P143]
And Cheongpung…

[P144]
“Hey! Where do you think you’re going?”

[P145]
“Gasp! Benefactor!”

[P146]
Was that bastard seriously trying to buy dumplings right now…?

[P147]

[P148]
*I’m definitely catching that bastard.*

[P149]

[P150]
But they weren’t the only Qingxia Hall martial artists present.

[P151]
“Ha-ha-ha! How amusing. Truly amusing. Don’t you agree?”

[P152]
At the young man’s laughing question, the four huge men carrying his palanquin answered in unison.

[P153]
“Yes, my lord.”

[P154]
“We cannot simply let the honored guest who gave this Young Master such a laugh leave. Do not worry about me. Go and escort him here.”

[P155]
“Loyalty!”

[P156]

[P157]
The mere palanquin bearers revealed themselves as formidable Peak masters. They claimed all four directions as they closed in.

[P158]
Whoooooosh!

[P159]
Each threw a punch carrying fierce qi, the four strikes interlocking with exquisite precision.

[P160]
Thud-thud-thud-thud!

[P163]
None of them got back up.

[P164]
“What the sibu-leol…?”

[P165]
“……!”

[P166]
“……!”

[P167]
“……!”

[P168]
Complete silence descended over the main road.

[P169]
I nudged the unconscious giants with my foot, then shrugged at the young man. The corners of his mouth, which had been raised so high moments before, were now trembling.

[P170]
“Interesting. Very interesting. Don’t you all agree?”

[P171]
The Zhuge Clan retainer put a hand to his forehead, while Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin nodded mechanically.

[P172]
“This is the most fun I’ve had in all my thirty years as a beggar.”

[P173]
“Captain, I laughed so hard my belly button fell off. I can’t see where it rolled, so I’m still looking for it.”

[P174]
“Right. In times as bleak as these, how could we simply let the man who gave us such wonderful entertainment leave? So…”

[P175]
I pointed at the young man.

[P176]
“Grab that bastard by the collar and escort him over here.”

[P177]
“Loyalty, loyalty!”

[P178]
“I give up. Whatever happens, you’ll deal with it yourself.”

[P179]
Hyuk Mujin, desperate to avoid even a single blow, threw himself into the task with greater enthusiasm than anyone else. Gung Gibang stepped forward as well, despite his grumbling.

[P180]
The situation had completely reversed.

[P181]
Once even their trusted guards were defeated, the men and women of Qingxia Hall began shrieking at the tops of their lungs.

[P182]
“Y-you bastard! Do you know who I am?”

[P183]
“You wretched scoundrel! How dare you defy the laws of the Great Nation!”

[P184]
“If you lay a hand on me, do you think my family will stand by and do nothing?”

[P185]
I had only meant to grab one of them, but apparently they were a set. The rest came attached.

[P186]
I turned to the first one who had shouted.

[P187]
“Who are you?”

[P188]
“I am the Young Bureau Head of the Daejuksan Escort Bureau…”

[P189]
“Oh, Juksan Escort Bureau?”

[P190]
“So you do know us!”

[P191]
“I don’t, you sibu-leol bastard. Get down before I beat you into juk.”[^1]

[P192]
They might have thrown their weight around in Hubei Province, but if I’d never heard of them, they were nobodies.

[P193]
I continued quietly.

[P194]
“Get down now, and I’ll only destroy the palanquin. Refuse, and I’ll destroy your legs along with it. What’ll it be?”

[P195]
The Young Bureau Head of the Daejuksan Escort Bureau widened his eyes and answered,

[P196]
“I’ll get down.”

[P197]
“You should’ve done that from the start. Why are your eyes so wide?”

[P198]
“I’m sorry. If I don’t do this, I think I might cry…”

[P199]
Ah. That was understandable.

[P200]
After putting him in his place, I turned to the sharp-voiced woman.

[P201]
“What family did you say you were from?”

[P202]
“H-hmph! No matter how much of a scoundrel you are, surely you’ve heard the name of the Hyungmun Sword Family!”

[P203]
“Never heard of it. Stop talking nonsense and get down.”

[P204]
“……!”

[P205]
“Next. Where are you from?”

[P206]
“I-I’m from the Eungseong Merchant Association…”

[P207]
“Eungseong, Eung-shit, whatever. Get down unless you want me to beat you until you crap yourself.”

[P208]
“Yes, sir.”

[P209]
After two or three of them climbed down from their palanquins, the rest quietly followed before I could even ask.

[P210]
All except one.

[P211]
“So, who are you?”

[P212]
Every trace of laughter had vanished from the young man’s face. His eyes gleamed coldly.

[P213]
“You have crossed a line you should never have crossed.”

[P214]
“Looks like you’ve crossed your lifeline too. So who are you?”

[P215]
“Heh. What a ridiculous situation.”

[P216]
The young man let out a hollow laugh, then proclaimed in a dignified voice,

[P217]
“I, Ju Wongong, am a noble scion of the dragon’s blood and a third cousin of His Imperial Majesty the Emperor! If you understand the gravity of your crime, kneel at once!”

[P218]
“Okay, Celestial Dragon.[^2] Get down.”

[P219]
“……!”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 453

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃453화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“야! 이 개애새끼들아아!”
  6|
  7|순간 차가운 바람이 불었던 것 같다. 아니면 내 고함이 그렇게 느껴질 만큼 우렁찼거나.
  8|
  9|아마 후자일 가능성이 크겠지.
 10|
 11|솨아아아아.
 12|
 13|은자를 줍기 위해 버둥거리던 수십 명의 사람이 움직임을 멈추고, 소란스러운 대로변에 침묵이 내려앉는다.
 14|
 15|그리고 다음 순간, 내 입술 사이로 흘러나온 한마디가 짧은 정적을 깨트렸다.
 16|
 17|“셋 센다.”
 18|
 19|“……?”
 20|
 21|“집합.”
 22|
 23|“……!”
 24|
 25|서당 개 삼 년이면 풍월을 읊고, 맞으면서 지내면 사서삼경도 외운다.
 26|
 27|그것이 지난 일 년 동안 내 폭력과 욕설에 길든 서당 개, 아니 혁무진이 누구보다 빠르게 움직일 수 있는 이유였다.
 28|
 29|“집하아압!”
 30|
 31|비명 같은 복명복창과 함께 달려온 혁무진의 신형이 내 앞에서 딱 멈췄다.
 32|
 33|이어 한 박자 늦게 사태를 파악하고 경신법을 발휘한 궁기방이 혁무진과 거의 동시에 도착했고, 청풍은…….
 34|
 35|“전병! 전병 빨리 주세요! 은인 화났어요!”
 36|
 37|시벌 놈이. 그 와중에 전병 챙기는 것 봐라.
 38|
 39|나는 군것질거리를 포장한 뒤 빛살처럼 달려오는 청풍을 향해 부드럽게 말했다.
 40|
 41|“천천히 와. 나 화 안 났으니까.”
 42|
 43|“와아! 정말요?”
 44|
 45|“응. 화난 게 아니라 존나 빡친 거야.”
 46|
 47|“앗, 아앗…….”
 48|
 49|나는 안절부절못하는 청풍과 슬그머니 시선을 회피하는 두 녀석을 바라보며 생각했다.
 50|
 51|‘도대체 이 자식들은 언제쯤 사람이 될까.’
 52|
 53|젖 먹던 힘까지 끌어 올려서 제갈세가로 달려가진 못할망정, 은자 몇 개 줍겠답시고 무공까지 쓰는 꼬락서니 봐라.
 54|
 55|심지어 궁기방 저놈은 은근슬쩍 다른 사람 손에 있던 은자까지 뺏었다. 이 정도면 거지가 아니라 도적놈이다.
 56|
 57|‘인생, 씨바…….’
 58|
 59|최근 사원 복지를 위해 애썼건만, 결국 이렇게 되는구나.
 60|
 61|맑은 하늘을 우러러본 나는 손바닥에 침을 뱉었다.
 62|
 63|“혁무진. 이마 대.”
 64|
 65|“예?”
 66|
 67|고개를 번쩍 든 혁무진이 황당한 표정으로 되물었다.
 68|
 69|“저만요?”
 70|
 71|“응. 우선 너만.”
 72|
 73|“궁 소협은요?”
 74|
 75|“쟨 뼛속까지 거지잖아. 솔직히 거지가 은자 줍는다는데 뭐라 하기도 그래.”
 76|
 77|“정확하고도 현명한 판단이로군.”
 78|
 79|눈치를 보고 있던 궁기방이 엄숙한 목소리로 끼어들자 혁무진이 고리눈을 떴다.
 80|
 81|“아니, 그렇긴 뭐가 그럽니까. 내가 거지라고 하면 맨날 화내면서.”
 82|
 83|“내가? 무슨 말도 안 되는 소릴. 나는 머리부터 발끝까지 거지다. 태어날 때부터 거지였고 죽을 때까지 거지로 살 거야.”
 84|
 85|“……거지 같네, 진짜.”
 86|
 87|“칭찬 고맙군.”
 88|
 89|“궁기방 거지새끼.”
 90|
 91|“허어, 이리도 감미로울 수가.”
 92|
 93|궁기방을 죽일 듯이 노려보던 혁무진이 재차 입을 열었다.
 94|
 95|“그럼 청 소협은요?”
 96|

“……”

[P131]
The Zhuge Clan retainer looked back and forth between me, standing there with my fist clenched, and the sparrow-eyed man, who lay unconscious with his nose crushed.

[P132]
He muttered awkwardly,

[P133]
“I said it might be best if you stopped…”

[P134]
“Pardon?”

[P135]
“There may be various complications…”

[P136]
“Pardon?”

[P137]
“It would be wise to avoid any unnecessary conflict…”

[P138]
“What was that?”

[P139]
“……Never mind.”

[P140]
“Ah. All right.”

[P141]
I wiped the blood from my fist on my trouser leg and looked around.

[P142]
Gung Gibang was muttering that he’d known the man would end up like that, while Hyuk Mujin beamed at his unexpected reprieve.

[P143]
And Cheongpung…

[P144]
“Hey! Where do you think you’re going?”

[P145]
“Gasp! Benefactor!”

[P146]
Was that bastard seriously trying to buy dumplings right now…?

[P147]
Cheongpung was silently inching away. Watching his retreating back, I began to wonder if he was really human.

[P148]
*I’m definitely catching that bastard.*

[P149]
I stepped forward with grim resolve. The ornamental guards surrounding us sucked in their breaths and moved aside.

[P150]
But they weren’t the only Qingxia Hall martial artists present.

[P151]
“Ha-ha-ha! How amusing. Truly amusing. Don’t you agree?”

[P152]
At the young man’s laughing question, the four huge men carrying his palanquin answered in unison.

[P153]
“Yes, my lord.”

[P154]
“We cannot simply let the honored guest who gave this Young Master such a laugh leave. Do not worry about me. Go and escort him here.”

[P155]
“Loyalty!”

[P156]
Their shout rang with internal energy. The huge men set down the palanquin and charged toward me with the speed of the wind.

[P157]
The mere palanquin bearers revealed themselves as formidable Peak masters. They claimed all four directions as they closed in.

[P158]
Whoooooosh!

[P159]
Each threw a punch carrying fierce qi, the four strikes interlocking with exquisite precision.

[P160]
Thud-thud-thud-thud!

[P161]
Exactly four impacts sounded.

[P162]
Four bodies hit the ground face-first with all the momentum of their charge.

[P163]
None of them got back up.

[P164]
“What the sibu-leol…?”

[P165]
“……!”

[P166]
“……!”

[P167]
“……!”

[P168]
Complete silence descended over the main road.

[P169]
I nudged the unconscious giants with my foot, then shrugged at the young man. The corners of his mouth, which had been raised so high moments before, were now trembling.

[P170]
“Interesting. Very interesting. Don’t you all agree?”

[P171]
The Zhuge Clan retainer put a hand to his forehead, while Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin nodded mechanically.

[P172]
“This is the most fun I’ve had in all my thirty years as a beggar.”

[P173]
“Captain, I laughed so hard my belly button fell off. I can’t see where it rolled, so I’m still looking for it.”

[P174]
“Right. In times as bleak as these, how could we simply let the man who gave us such wonderful entertainment leave? So…”

[P175]
I pointed at the young man.

[P176]
“Grab that bastard by the collar and escort him over here.”

[P177]
“Loyalty, loyalty!”

[P178]
“I give up. Whatever happens, you’ll deal with it yourself.”

[P179]
Hyuk Mujin, desperate to avoid even a single blow, threw himself into the task with greater enthusiasm than anyone else. Gung Gibang stepped forward as well, despite his grumbling.

[P180]
The situation had completely reversed.

[P181]
Once even their trusted guards were defeated, the men and women of Qingxia Hall began shrieking at the tops of their lungs.

[P182]
“Y-you bastard! Do you know who I am?”

[P183]
“You wretched scoundrel! How dare you defy the laws of the Great Nation!”

[P184]
“If you lay a hand on me, do you think my family will stand by and do nothing?”

[P185]
I had only meant to grab one of them, but apparently they were a set. The rest came attached.

[P186]
I turned to the first one who had shouted.

[P187]
“Who are you?”

[P188]
“I am the Young Bureau Head of the Daejuksan Escort Bureau…”

[P189]
“Oh, Juksan Escort Bureau?”

[P190]
“So you do know us!”

[P191]
“I don’t, you sibu-leol bastard. Get down before I beat you into juk.”[^1]

[P192]
They might have thrown their weight around in Hubei Province, but if I’d never heard of them, they were nobodies.

[P193]
I continued quietly.

[P194]
“Get down now, and I’ll only destroy the palanquin. Refuse, and I’ll destroy your legs along with it. What’ll it be?”

[P195]
The Young Bureau Head of the Daejuksan Escort Bureau widened his eyes and answered,

[P196]
“I’ll get down.”

[P197]
“You should’ve done that from the start. Why are your eyes so wide?”

[P198]
“I’m sorry. If I don’t do this, I think I might cry…”

[P199]
Ah. That was understandable.

[P200]
After putting him in his place, I turned to the sharp-voiced woman.

[P201]
“What family did you say you were from?”

[P202]
“H-hmph! No matter how much of a scoundrel you are, surely you’ve heard the name of the Hyungmun Sword Family!”

[P203]
“Never heard of it. Stop talking nonsense and get down.”

[P204]
“……!”

[P205]
“Next. Where are you from?”

[P206]
“I-I’m from the Eungseong Merchant Association…”

[P207]
“Eungseong, Eung-shit, whatever. Get down unless you want me to beat you until you crap yourself.”

[P208]
“Yes, sir.”

[P209]
After two or three of them climbed down from their palanquins, the rest quietly followed before I could even ask.

[P210]
All except one.

[P211]
“So, who are you?”

[P212]
Every trace of laughter had vanished from the young man’s face. His eyes gleamed coldly.

[P213]
“You have crossed a line you should never have crossed.”

[P214]
“Looks like you’ve crossed your lifeline too. So who are you?”

[P215]
“Heh. What a ridiculous situation.”

[P216]
The young man let out a hollow laugh, then proclaimed in a dignified voice,

[P217]
“I, Ju Wongong, am a noble scion of the dragon’s blood and a third cousin of His Imperial Majesty the Emperor! If you understand the gravity of your crime, kneel at once!”

[P218]
“Okay, Celestial Dragon.[^2] Get down.”

[P219]
“……!”

[P220]
[^1]: *Juk* is Korean rice porridge, continuing Taekyung’s wordplay on “Juksan.”
[^2]: The privileged World Nobles in *One Piece*, infamous for treating ordinary people as beneath them.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
